limits: Explicit callbacks are selected Rust copy policies, not native API parameters or automatic arbitrary C++ copy/lifetime/address-sensitive dispatch.
Panic traces model the observed copy exceptions, not arbitrary exception type/message, ABI or noexcept behavior.
Outer wrapper lock scopes narrow native reentrant and aliased access; callbacks must avoid reentering the wrapper lock. The fixture observes canonical metadata through the existing observer.

Native allocator subclass callbacks and physical allocation sizes/policies are not ported by this batch. Logical live allocation and publication/release order are verified; allocation failure itself remains unproved.
The older consuming append convenience remains available but is no longer the binding target for native const-reference Append.
No complete class, implicit special-member, inherited API, RTTI/alias or denominator-complete proof is claimed.
allocator_observation: Native custom BaseAllocator counts successful Allocate/Free calls. Rust reads real live typed-allocation counts from the incremental allocator checked-reset diagnostic; no fake node engine or mirrored count is used. Successful zero-live reset only rewinds empty storage. Canonical SequenceObserver reads size during construction without reentering the outer wrapper lock. These observations prove logical allocation/publication/release phases, not identical underlying heap-policy callbacks, byte requests or retained memory.
